- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) or trending negative, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope after peak.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates near-term upside — cap forecast growth at 3–5% above recent 7-day average.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — add 1–2% buffer to forecast if sentiment swings >0.2 in last 5 days.
- When sentiment is flat or mildly negative, model shows persistent lag — forecast should be adjusted to match recent 14-day moving average, not 30-day trend.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after 2–3 consecutive peaks), model often fails to recognize — reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
